title: Hoagy Carmichael, Stardust and Trumbauer's influence
summary: Challis agrees Hoagy absorbed Bix and Trumbauer in Stardust, praises his early tunes, and Gitler mentions Lester Young.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: What do you think about this has been advanced by somebody, I don't remember who about the effect of Bix on Hoagy Carmichael, that some of the songs that Hoagy wrote were really things he heard Bix play and he took those.
I think his Stardust is a little --
It's been said of that. Do you agree with that?
I agree with it to a certain extent, yes. He did a lot of that. Hoagy and I used to be very close.

He did -- I remember when he was doing that and before he got lyrics, he was crazy about (sings) , now that's Trumbauer's part, see. (sings) that's Bix's, see. Now, then Hoagy, he comes in "(Stardust)" you know, it sounds a lot --

It seems like he absorbed a little bit of Trumbauer and Bix to do something like that, although I think he's great. Hoagy, especially his early stuff. I did a lot of his early things with him. I mean arranging. I particularly liked the way he did "Washboard Blues." I think he's a real American composer; but he -- naturally he got commercial later on, but the way, our business, the way it is, you can't blame a guy for getting commercial. He's going to starve if he doesn't get commercial somehow or other.
Even some of his later hits like "Buttermilk Sky," it had a very good melody.
Well, he couldn't do anything bad. "Up A Lazy River." He wrote a lot of good tunes and there was one that never got around was "One Night in the band." Did you ever hear of that one?
That was quite nice. [Paul] Mertz tells me it's recorded by somebody, but I don't know. I like Hoagy, I like his work.
But you would say he was generally
influenced by growing up and being part of that whole period.
Of course, but he added something to it on his own.
But he certainly liked Bix and he liked Trumbauer and he liked those choruses. I think they had somewhat of --
Everybody who listened to those -- of course, the famous story of Lester Young, told hearing "Singing the Blues" and that's --
In his style he was very influenced by Trumbauer, but I think everybody was influenced by Trumbauer, all the saxophone players.
